title: Spin Splitter without Spin-Split Bands: A Reconfigurable Altermagnetic Texture
authors: Bin Xi, Jie Lu, Qiang Luo, Ken Chen, Jia-Wei Mei, Hong-Gang Luo, Jize Zhao
abstract: The altermagnetic spin-splitter effect converts an electric field into a transverse pure spin current, with no net magnetization and no charge-Hall counterpart. In established materials this function is tied to crystal-fixed spin-split bands that lock the polarization axis to the lattice. We show that the noncoplanar counter-spiral ground state of a frustrated honeycomb magnet instead carries the altermagnetic operation through a $\mathbf Q$-locked helicity mirror $g$. The mirror selects the spin-current polarization and forbids the perpendicular one, while an antitranslation $Θ$ forbids even-parity spin splitting. Band splitting and spin-splitter response therefore rest on different symmetry elements. Either element alone enforces the charge-Hall zero---a redundancy absent from other spin--orbit-free noncollinear routes---and a charge Hall appears only when both elements are removed. Hole doping then realizes a \emph{spin splitter without spin-split bands}---the symmetry-allowed odd-parity residual below $2\times10^{-7}$ of the hopping $t$ at the Fermi level---with $σ_H^{(s_y)}=0.082\,e^2/h$ without spin--orbit coupling and with zero charge Hall response. Selecting among the three degenerate $\mathbf{Q}$ orientations rotates the polarization axis in exact $120^\circ$ steps at fixed magnitude and charge-Hall zero; the selection rules persist in a $32$-site cell accessible to programmable photonic and circuit lattices.
summary: This theoretical study proposes a novel mechanism for realizing the spin splitter effect in altermagnetic materials by exploiting symmetry constraints rather than relying on traditional band splitting. By analyzing a frustrated honeycomb magnet, the authors show that hole doping can induce this pure spin current response while maintaining zero charge Hall conductivity. This work is significant because it provides a robust, symmetry-protected route to engineered topological transport phenomena.
main_problem: The research aims to demonstrate a spin-splitter effect—converting an electric field into a pure transverse spin current without charge response—in altermagnetic materials without relying on conventional crystal-fixed spin-split bands.
main_result: Hole doping in the model realizes this spin splitter using an odd-parity residual, achieving a finite spin Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{sy}^H=0.082\,e^2/h$) while maintaining zero charge Hall response ($\sigma_{ch}^{xy}=0$).
method: The analysis uses symmetry constraints derived from specific Spin-Space-Group elements (an antitranslation $\Theta$ and a helicity mirror $g$) applied to an $s$-$d$ Hamiltonian describing itinerant electrons coupled to a classical spin texture.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a frustrated honeycomb magnet exhibiting a noncoplanar counter-spiral ground state. The physics is analyzed by examining how the symmetry elements $\Theta$ and $g$ constrain band splitting and transport responses.
key_observables: Spin-splitter conductivity ($\sigma_{sy}^H$), Charge Hall response ($\sigma_{ch}^{xy}$), Band splitting ($\Delta(k)$), and polarization axis rotation angle ($120^\circ$).
important_parameters: The residual hopping term (odd-parity) below $2	imes 10^{-7} t$ at the Fermi level, and the specific value $\sigma_{sy}^H = 0.082\,e^2/h$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes coupling itinerant electrons to a preformed classical spin texture via an $s$-$d$ Hamiltonian, and that the symmetry constraints ($\Theta$ and $g$) are robustly applicable.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the counter-spiral magnetization texture, the calculated signed band splitting $\Delta(k)$ showing small spectral separation, and plots demonstrating the finite spin Hall conductivity at optimal doping while keeping the charge Hall zero.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework by identifying symmetry elements ($\Theta$ and $g$) that govern altermagnetism. It then develops the core argument that these symmetries dictate transport properties, culminating in the crucial finding about hole doping realizing the spin splitter without band splitting, followed by discussions on reconfigurability.
why_interesting: The work provides a deep symmetry-based understanding of topological magnetotransport phenomena, showing how fundamental crystalline symmetries can enforce exotic quantum responses (like zero charge Hall response) even when spectral features are suppressed. This links condensed matter theory to programmable physical platforms like photonics.
